guion_largo.texto:
A palace is not always a place of luxury. In Xochicalco, the one the INAH calls the Palace has a more practical air.

According to the INAH, the Palace is located on the middle level of the city. It is a complex of rooms, kitchens, workshops, storerooms, and a temazcal, organized around courtyards.

A temazcal is a steam bath. It was used to cleanse the body and also in ceremonies. According to Andrews and Glascock, there were temazcals in the Acropolis and in the northern sector. That is why you will see one also in [the north complex](xoc_20_agua_ritual_norte).

Medina Romero mentions that this palace and the La Malinche complex form a residential complex south of the city.

Think about that mix of spaces. Cooking, storing, working, and resting were all together, around a single courtyard. It is more of a complex where people lived, cooked, and worked.

This does not mean it was a palace like that of a European king. The word palace is a label used by archaeologists. What the remains show are living quarters, courtyards, and work areas.

To understand where the rulers lived, you have to climb up to [the Acropolis](xoc_17_acropolis). There stood, according to Hirth, the ruler’s palace and the administrative center of the city.

For now, sweep the courtyards with your eyes and see how many rooms open onto each one.

texto: Count the courtyards you can see
Look for spaces that could have been kitchens or storerooms
Imagine who worked and who slept in each room

texto.Spaces: rooms, kitchens, workshops, storerooms, and temazcal, around courtyards
texto.Residential complex: with La Malinche, south of the city, according to Medina Romero

texto.pregunta: Myth: The Palace was the ruler’s house.
texto.respuesta: Reality: It is the name archaeologists give to a complex of rooms, kitchens, workshops, and storerooms. The ruler’s residence is associated with the Acropolis.
